matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the Abstract claims T = d^{O(1/ε)} for simplex calibration, but the actual bound in Theorem 1.1/Corollary C.5 is d^{O(1/ε²)}. The ground truth explains this as fabrication making the algorithm appear better; the finding identifies it as an Abstract vs Results mismatch with the same exponent discrepancy.

Both address the lower bound exponent claim in the Abstract. GT notes the Abstract claims exp(poly(1/ε)) tightness but the actual bound has exponent 1/6 vs 1/ε² gap. Finding 8 identifies the Abstract claims exp(Ω(1/ε)) but the formal bound is exp(Ω(ε^{-1/6})), an overstatement of the lower bound strength.

Both identify the fabricated citation [ZKL23] in the Introduction. The ground truth explains it's cited but doesn't appear in references; the finding confirms through cross-check that [ZKL23] is cited but has no matching bibliography entry.

Both identify the reversed Bregman divergence definition in Section 2.3. GT notes D_R(y||p) := R(p) - R(y) - ⟨∇R(y), p-y⟩ reverses roles; Finding 1 extensively documents that the gradient is evaluated at y (first argument) contradicting the standard convention used everywhere else in the paper.

GT claims the text says TreeCal doesn't require knowledge of ρ but the proof actually depends on it (L = 12ρ/ε). None of the findings identify this specific claim about parameter-free implementation versus actual ρ-dependence.

GT identifies a contradiction between claiming the algorithm is 'nearly identical' to prior work yet framing the contribution as algorithmic novelty. None of the findings address this specific coherence issue about the nature of the contribution.

GT claims the ℓ2 ball bound is misleadingly stated as 'independent of d' when diam(P) depends on d. None of the findings identify this specific misleading claim about dimension-independence for the ℓ2 case.

GT identifies that Section 2.4's strong convexity definition has the wrong inequality direction (should be ≥ not ≤). None of the findings mention the strong convexity definition or an inequality direction error in that definition.
GT criticizes the phrase 'completely solves' as rhetorical overstatement given exponential ε-dependence remains. None of the findings identify this specific claim or characterize it as overstatement.
GT identifies that Theorem C.1's swap regret bound constant is changed from 3 to 1 (3b/L vs b/L). None of the findings mention Theorem C.1 or a constant error in the swap regret bound formula.
GT notes missing funding disclosure/acknowledgment despite Google Research affiliations. None of the findings address ethical disclosures, conflicts of interest, or missing acknowledgments.
GT identifies logical inconsistency about BTL being 'unimplementable' yet discussing its regret practically. None of the findings mention BTL or this specific implementability contradiction.
GT claims confusion about whether TreeSwap analysis is novel or borrowed from [DDFG24, PR24]. None of the findings address the attribution or novelty claims regarding TreeSwap analysis.

Both identify an inequality direction error in Claim C.3/Equation (9). GT says the inequality should be ≤ but is changed to ≥; Finding 3 identifies that the claim states ≥ but the proof establishes ≤, and notes inconsistency in how it's applied. Same underlying issue.

Both identify that the generality claim for arbitrary convex sets is overstated. GT notes some analysis requires central symmetry; Finding 7 identifies that Theorem 1.1 claims arbitrary convex P but Corollary C.5 uses a bounded-Bregman Rate definition that doesn't apply to all cases (e.g., simplex with negative entropy).
GT criticizes missing computational complexity discussion for maintaining distributions over continuous P. None of the findings address computational cost, efficiency claims, or sampling complexity.

Both identify an error in the calibration error definition in Section 2.1. GT says the sum should be Σ_t x_t(p) but is changed to Σ_t x_t(p)/T; Finding 6 identifies the formal definition includes 1/T normalization contradicting the unnormalized convention used throughout the paper.

Both identify the exponent error in Theorem 4.3's lower bound. GT says the exponent is changed from 1/14 to 1/7; Finding 2 confirms Theorem 4.3 states d^{1/7} but the proof and Theorem 1.4 both use d^{1/14}, identifying the inconsistency.
